Now when the Greeks heard that Diogenes had been captured,
they proclaimed for themselves as king Michael the son of Constantine.
And he seized his mother,
she who was the wife of Diogenes,
and by force placed her in a monastery.
And his paternal uncle John became Caesar to him.
Now when {OCR?} Diogenes entered the territory of the Romans,
and heard what had happened,
he went up to the fortress of Dokeia.
And he found in it two hundred thousand dinars,
and he sent them to the Sultan with those two emirs who had gone with him,
and informed him of the matter.
And he put on the habit of monasticism,
and dwelt in Dokeia.
And he sent to Michael and said:
"Up to now I have fought the good fight on behalf of the confession {OCR?} of the Christians,
and it is enough for me.
As for you, blessed is your kingdom,
and you have done well that you have reigned,
because it was fitting for you.
However, I faithfully advise you not to dissolve the peace which I made with the Sultan,
otherwise no rest will remain,
neither for you,
nor for {OCR?} the Christians."
And Michael accepted his kindness (or: thanked him) and said:
"I will not depart from your counsel."
Now after some days certain men worked upon him,
and he sent to Diogenes and said to him:
"If in truth you are a monk,
why do you have a residence in a fortress? It is fitting that you go down to one of the monasteries,
so that we may send guards into the fortress."
Then Diogenes became furious and said:
"Out of the whole kingdom of the Romans he does not leave me even one fortress!"
And he arose and stripped off the woollen garments,
and took the wealth of the merchants of Dokeia by way of a loan,
and gathered for himself an army.
And when the son of Sennacherib, the Patrician of Lesser Armenia, came to him,
he seized him and plucked out his eyes,
and took from him eighty centenaria of gold.
And he grew very strong and came to Melitene,
and sent to the Sultan Alp Arslan,
and asked for help from him.
And the Sultan promised him,
that he in person would go and help him wherever the occasion called for it.
And after these things,
Diogenes departed from Melitene to {OCR?} Cilicia.
And John came against him,
and besieged him in the city of Adana.
And when he captured him,
he sent and informed King Michael.
